capability: Nobody in the roster owns the studio's own operating tools. Studio/jarvis/build-jarvis.py is 1,700 lines that every founder decision is now read through, and no agent produces it, maintains it, or holds a write grant covering the directory it lives in.
evidence: Studio/constitution/permissions.json -- no grant's write or append list contains any path under Studio/jarvis/
Studio/constitution/org.json -- no division's writeScope covers Studio/jarvis/**
Studio/constitution/agents/*.json -- across all 100 records, zero agents name Studio/jarvis in writeScope, tools or measurableOutput
Studio/jarvis/build-jarvis.py -- exists, is regenerated by hand, and its --check validator is run by no gate
Studio/build/gate-g2.sh -- runs check-core-purity, check-forbidden-remedies, check-write-scope and generate-agent-definitions --check; it does not run build-jarvis.py --check

consideredExisting.whyNot: Its tools already include run:generate-agent-definitions.sh, so a second generator looks like a fit. But its successMetric is about dormant agents whose precondition has been met, and its measurableOutput is registry consistency. Widening it to own a rendering tool would give it two unrelated success metrics, which is the shape the duplicate-metric check exists to prevent.

Owns assembly definitions, package manifests and the compile-time structure the dual-compile verification depends on. Studio/jarvis compiles nothing and is not part of any assembly; its output is a page, and its correctness is a rendering and honesty question rather than a toolchain one.

Could plausibly wire build-jarvis.py --check into a gate, and should. But .github/workflows and Studio/build are human-exclusive paths it may not write, and running a check is not the same as owning what the check validates.

Reads the cockpit and is arguably its main consumer, but is a boss tier that coordinates rather than builds, and giving the consumer of a report ownership of the tool that generates it removes the separation that makes the report worth reading.

whyExistingRosterIsInsufficient: Activation does not answer this one, which is the first thing to rule out and the usual answer. All 70 dormant records were carved for game-production capabilities -- audio, content, live-ops, growth, compliance, analytics -- and none of them describes studio-internal tooling; there is no dormant agent whose activatesWhen could ever fire for this. Widening an existing scope was examined agent by agent above and each candidate would acquire a second, unrelated success metric. Leaving the work unowned is the status quo, and the status quo is what produced an unversioned page nobody validates in CI.
notes: Filed as open rather than proposed on purpose. The gap is established by the evidence above; the right answer is not. A studio-tooling specialist is one option, and folding Studio/jarvis into a widened studio-ops grant with an existing owner is another and cheaper one. Deciding that is an L1 call for the chief executive, and creation of any new agent is a Studio/constitution edit, which is human-exclusive under permissions.json regardless of who proposes it. This record grants no authority to do either -- see ADR-0005.
